newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall as interest rate pressure mounts.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall as interest rate pressure mounts.

text.p: Stocks tumbled Friday in a continuation of Thursday's sell-off as a weaker bond market intensified pressure on blue chips.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 50.80 points at 6,704.95, after falling almost 80 points earlier. On Thursday, the blue-chip index rose above the 6,900 level for the first time before ending down 94.28 points.
In the broader market, declining issues outpaced gainers by 16 to seven on very heavy volume of 309 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

In the bond market, the bellwether 30-year Treasury bond fell 18/32, or $5.625 on a $1,000 bond, sending its yield up to 6.90 percent from 6.86 percent at Thursday's close. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.
"The one big negative is that interest rates are over 6.90 percent," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "That's a cause of concern for the market."
The interest rate-sensitive financial sector was particularly hard hit during the sell-off.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Bank index fell 8.09 points, or 1.42 percent, to 560.46, with 23 of the 24 stocks listed in the index posting losses.

"It's very hard to ignore the fact that rates continue to go up and you have to worry about forward earnings for the banks with higher rates," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Technology stocks were also broadly lower, with computer networking stocks suffering the steepest declines.
The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index was down 11.11 points to 1,367.26.
Cascade Communications Corp. plummeted 21-1/8 to 43 a day after the company reported fourth-quarter results.
While Cascade's earnings were sharply higher than a year ago, several analysts downgraded the shares Friday, citing concerns about slow growth at the company's core network switching business.
Shares in several networking equipment companies got caught in the selling pressure, among them Ascend Communications Inc., off 1-7/8 to 73-7/8.
Industry leader Cisco Systems Inc. fell 3 to 68-3/4.
Despite signs that the weakness in stocks was broadening, some analysts saw the back-tracking as aiding the long-term health of the bull market.
"These kinds of setbacks are good because they cause people to reevaluate and scare away speculative froth," said Tom Carpenter, chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc.
Among individual issues, RDO Equipment Co. jumped 2-5/8 to 18-1/8 in their first day of trading. The company owns and operates John Deere industrial stores and agricultural stores.
Singer Co. fell 4-1/2 to 17-1/8 after reporting a fourth-quarter loss. Singer also said it would exit the furniture manufacturing business in the United States.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks shed 5.21 to 772.35.
